speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth in light of the recent cancellation of Art Stage Singapore shortly before it was due to open (a) how has the National Arts Council helped the affected exhibitors; and (b) what is being done to support the viability of holding art fairs in Singapore moving forward.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Art Stage Singapore was a commercial art fair first organised in 2011.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The National Arts Council (NAC), Singapore Tourism Board (STB) and Economic Development Board (EDB) supported the event through raising international awareness of Singapore’s art offerings, growing a strong local and regional collector base, and building local capability for art market development.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: However, we are not privy to commercial information of Art Stage, nor do we share in its commercial risk.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MCCY and NAC were disappointed and saddened by the decision of the Art Stage organisers to cancel the 2019 edition at short notice.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Other organisations also stepped forward to offer assistance, including private galleries and non-profit spaces in Singapore, such as Gajah Gallery, PLOT, The Culture Story, Japan Creative Centre, and Marina Bay Sands.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This was a demonstration of the strong spirit of the arts community in Singapore, and the close partnership among the public, private and people sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: An international media outlet called it “a triumph of community spirit”.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: NAC promoted all their exhibitions as part of Singapore Art Week.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As outlined in NAC's Our SG Arts Plan, our aspiration is for Singapore to be recognised globally as the visual arts city for Southeast Asian art.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: To achieve this objective, NAC has welcomed ideas and participation from a wide range of partners, including those from the private sector.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These ideas help us to innovate and bring different offerings to serve the local and global arts fraternity and enable Singapore to distinguish itself from the others.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As is the nature of innovation, some ideas take off, others do not.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In working with commercial partners, it would not be appropriate for the Government to use taxpayers' money to underwrite all the risks.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Art Stage's cancellation was a disappointment for Singapore's art sector.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In fact, the efforts of many parties to deal with the aftermath demonstrate the depth and breadth of the network of the arts fraternity in Singapore, and the camaraderie among our arts community.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: It reinforces the progress that we have made to develop a healthy and vibrant arts ecosystem in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MCCY and NAC will continue to foster a vibrant and robust visual arts landscape in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We continue to welcome ideas and activities that show a deep understanding of, and engagement with, our arts stakeholders, and a commitment to connect with Singaporean audiences.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Minister mentioned that it is the view of the Government that art fairs on the scale of Art Stage are still viable going forward.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Given the cancellation of the recent Art Stage and also the declining number of exhibitors for Art Stage in the years prior to the year it was cancelled, there would appear to be some concerns.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Some concerns have been expressed about the lack of a local collector base, for example, to support visual arts events of the scale that Art Stage attempted to do.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will the Government agencies be pursuing any different strategies or be doing anything different to ensure the viability of future events, given some of these concerns in the recent past and also what we have seen with the cancellation?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: My second question is really on whether the Government will consider having some kind of early warning system.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If there had been a cancellation with more lead time, perhaps it would not have been so disruptive and so damaging to Singapore's branding as an arts hub.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Would the Government consider having or requiring some kind of early warning system where these commercial organisers have to issue alerts or have to provide updates on the finances of the events well prior to the date of the event starting?

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: In this process, we welcome participation, ideas and suggestions, and I am sure many of these commercial players would take viability into consideration.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We are hopeful and optimistic about Singapore as an arts market.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Whether there will be another Art Stage and in what form, it is early days to comment.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: As I said, we are always open to suggestions and proposals from commercial players.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: And even in the few media meetings that we had, there was no inkling about plans to cancel the show.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: Like all commercial entities, financial situations are not something they would openly display or share with the public.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is also not something we ask of participants.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: It is important for us to always remember that the art marketplace is not one where the regulator itself can decide its viability, and its growth requires all the parties in the visual arts landscape to play their part.

speaker: Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien
text: We call on the arts community to come in and support Singapore Art Week and any subsequent shows that we may have in Singapore.
